title: Pitch-class bracelets in 3D, transposed on the CPU or in TSL
question: Drawing all 4,096 pitch-class sets as 3D bracelets of 12 beads (49,152 instances), and animating a transposition that turns every bracelet by one semitone, is it cheaper to rewrite instance matrices and colors on the CPU each frame or to pass the step as a uniform to a TSL shader?
hypothesis: The CPU path pays for 49,152 matrix compositions and a 3 MB upload per frame; the TSL path uploads one float. The images are the same.

predictions.metric: median CPU ms per frame, CPU path, 4,096 bracelets
median CPU ms per frame, TSL path, 4,096 bracelets
